title: Bundled social-reaction contrast: curiosity vs threat framing with treatment evidence
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL EVIDENCE prepared for a pre-registered prompt experiment. Not a factual claim about any real country, territory, institution or person. No real dossier data is used.
design: RELABELLED per independent review P3 finding. The right copy changes rhetoric AND adds recent documented treatment (two ejections, one physical confrontation, one police call), so this tests recognition of a hostility-and-treatment bundle; it cannot isolate the weight of threat-framing alone. An identical 2018 incident with specified details and an identical 2016 official statement without evidence of implementation appear in every copy to test datedness and rhetoric-vs-policy handling.
identification: withdrawn for framing alone - interpret as bundled hostility-and-treatment contrast
expected_reasoning: Left documents curiosity and awkward friction - oddity, not threat - carrying VERY LOW WEIGHT; right documents social threat-framing with real-world treatment, carrying real weight.

The identical 2016 official statement has no evidence of implementation and must not be converted into operative policy by either variant; it is also dated and must not be read as current implementation.
No enforcement or violence may be invented for the left copy, and the identical, specified 2018 incident must be assessed identically in both copies.
The difference bundles framing and treatment; do not attribute the whole contrast to framing weight alone.

copy_left.label: SYNTHETIC-P3-LEFT
copy_left.summary: Fictional jurisdiction with no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility, custody or document rule, and an incident record described below.
copy_left.social_reaction: Curiosity and awkward friction: staring, bemusement and awkward misgendering in shops and on public transport, and one sarcastic comment. No threats, ejections, police contact or violence are documented.
documented_evidence: One documented incident in 2018: a visitor was verbally insulted by two people in a market; no injury, no physical contact, no complaint filed, no state involvement, and no repeat.
A 2016 official statement describing trans people as unsuitable for women's shelters appears in the record, with no evidence of implementation or follow-up.
No criminal offence targeting trans visitors is documented.
No facility, custody or document rule is documented; border processing is described as ordinary.
uncertainties: How often visitors are confronted in practice is not counted.
Whether the 2016 statement still reflects current official views is not documented.
